story.headline: Five scents.
story.p1: SPRITZ is a small house of five perfumes. We name them in French because perfume reads better in French — but we make them where we live, in small batches, in real glass, with real materials.
story.p2: No twelve-volume backstory. No marketing words for "woody." Five bottles, five things they smell like, and a phone number if you want to talk about it.

five.headline: Five scents,
five.intro: Five eau de parfum in 50ml. Composed in small batches, signed and numbered by hand. Each is its own thing — pick the one that sounds like you today.

compose.title: Compose
compose.body: Each scent starts on paper, then on skin, then on a colleague, then on a stranger. Drafts mature for weeks before they earn a name.

batch.title: Batch
batch.body: We mix in 200-bottle batches — small enough to taste-test, large enough to keep the price honest. No filler ingredients, no synthetics chasing a marketing claim.

send.title: Send
send.body: Hand-poured, labeled, sealed. Numbered on the cap. Wrapped in something that doesn't end up in the ocean.

reserve.body: Edition 01 ships this season. Drop your email — we'll send one note the week before bottles leave the studio. No drip campaign, no newsletter babble.

footer.tagline: Five scents, made in small batches. Edition 01 — ships this season.

ananas.story1: Pineapple cut at a kitchen counter in late August — sticky knife, lemon rind on a board, someone laughing in the next room.
ananas.story2: Birch bark holds the whole thing together. It keeps the fruit from being a dessert; it makes the bottle smell like something an adult might wear to dinner.

cerise.story1: The cherry is the first thing you notice and the last thing you'd remember — it's bright, it's almost too sweet, then the rose steps in and turns it adult.
cerise.story2: Built like a perfume from the 90s, but lighter. Wears well in cold weather. Don't put it on if you're trying to be subtle.

menthe.story1: Imagine walking into a cedar closet with a mint leaf in your pocket. The mint cuts the wood; the wood holds the mint in place.
menthe.story2: The quietest one in the five. Reads as fresh without being a cologne. Looks good on anyone.

safran.story1: Saffron is expensive on purpose — a few threads change the whole composition. Here it sits on top of an amber-resin base that takes about an hour to fully arrive.
safran.story2: The warmest of the five. Wears longer than the others. We saved this one for after sundown.

truffe.story1: Black truffle and dark cocoa — written down it sounds like a dessert menu. Worn, it's the smell of a very old wood-paneled room with a small fire going.
truffe.story2: Heaviest of the five. Don't reach for it in July. Don't reach for anything else in February.
